content.comment_body: Hello! I am looking for guidance on adding my extension module [product_name] (article no. [article_no]) to my already functioning base module ([product_name], article no. [article_no]). I have physically connected the extension to the base module but do not see the extension outputs available in [product_name] [product_name] [version_no]. How can I work with these outputs? Thank you.

There is no dedicated hardware configuration like you find in other systems. Once you dock the analog expansion module, the base module will detect if the expansion is powered. If it is the only expansion module, it will have the addresses AI1 and AI2.

I only have digital outputs. The main module provides four digital outputs labeled q1 to q4, and my extension has another four: q1 to q4. When I use output q5 in my diagram, it does not function as expected, so I think I am missing an important step.

Addressing for digital expansion modules follows a sequential scheme. For the base module: Inputs are I1 to I8 and outputs are Q1 to Q4. For the first expansion module, if using a DM8: Inputs become I9 to I12, and outputs Q5 to Q8. For DM16 modules: Inputs I9 to I16, outputs Q5 to Q12. If your expansion module is not operational, check these points: - Does it have a 24VDC supply? - What color is the RUN/STOP LED? Green means operation; red indicates you should check the contact slider is fully to the left. If the module works, verify your output wiring and use the online test tool to confirm if the program sets the output to 1.
It turned out the issue was with supply voltage. After correcting it, the expansion outputs work as intended. The problem has been resolved. Thank you for your assistance!

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered confusion when integrating a [product_name] digital expansion module with a base module using [product_name] [product_name]. The main difficulty involved identifying additional outputs in the software and understanding hardware addressing. Users also learned that proper hardware connection, especially supply voltage, was necessary for the expansion module to appear and function.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expected the digital expansion module outputs to immediately show up and be accessible in [product_name] [product_name] after installation. They assumed the software would auto-update to include the expansion module and provide sequential output addressing.
